exposure: mode of delivery (elective vs. non-elective cesarean section)
cohort: 2,767 women with singleton pregnancy who underwent uneventful cesarean section (defined as clinical estimation of intra-operative bleeding < 1000 ml)
finding: Non-elective cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of hemoglobin decline and blood product transfusion even in an apparently uneventful operation.
mod_finding: Non-elective cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of hemoglobin decline and blood product transfusion compared to elective cesarean section.
